description: Lowercase source text rendered with text-transform: uppercase so every glyph is uppercased before shaping.
Uppercase source text rendered with text-transform: lowercase so every glyph is lowercased before shaping.
Lowercase words rendered with text-transform: capitalize so the first letter of each word is uppercased.
An @font-face rule registering a second custom family ('ParityCustom') from the bundled ParitySerif TTF via src: url(), exercising the @font-face declaration and family-matching mechanism.
Mixed-case text rendered with font-variant: small-caps so lowercase letters become synthesized small uppercase forms.
Text with font-feature-settings: "liga" 0 to disable standard ligatures before shaping.
Two @font-face rules share a family but map normal and condensed stretch descriptors to visibly different bundled faces; both variants must select the matching face.
font-size: 2em resolved against the parent region's 16px font-size for a 32px effective size.
font-size: 2rem resolved against the root 16px font-size (32px), independent of the local 10px font-size.
font-size: 150% resolved against the parent region's 20px font-size for a 30px effective size.
font-size: 4ex resolves against the parent ParitySans face's used x-height; Fontations measures 11px at the 20px parent size, yielding 44px.
font-size: 5ch sized relative to the parent ParityMono face's '0' advance.
font-variant-caps:small-caps synthesizes smaller uppercase forms for lowercase letters; catches implementations that ignore font variant caps.
An @font-face rule aliases local ParitySerif and then uses that alias for a line of text. Catches: A url-only @font-face extractor passes relative URL fixtures but ignores local() sources.

Two @font-face rules share a family name but map normal to ParitySerif and bold to ParitySans; font-weight:bold must select the bold descriptor face. Catches: A parser that ignores descriptors registers one family/source and passes simple custom-font fixtures but chooses the wrong face for bold text.

A shared @font-face family maps normal to ParitySans and italic to ParitySerif; font-style:italic selects the italic descriptor source. Catches: Ignoring font-style descriptors passes a single-face @font-face test but cannot match style-specific faces.

Two @font-face rules share a family; uppercase A comes from ParitySerif and uppercase B from ParitySans via unicode-range. Catches: A font registry that ignores unicode-range passes ordinary fallback tests but renders all glyphs from one face.
With only a regular bundled face available, font-weight:600 should synthesize a visibly heavier weight than 400. Catches implementations that collapse only 700+ to bold.

Nested spans use bolder and lighter relative to a 600-weight parent, producing visibly different weights. Catches: A normal/bold-only parser treats bolder/lighter as normal and passes absolute weight fixtures.

A word uses font-style:oblique 20deg and visibly shears to the authored angle while a normal reference remains upright. The standards-derived reference materializes CSS Fonts 4's required specified-angle geometric fallback because Chromium computes the value but prints the regular-only face upright. Catches: Recognizing only the bare oblique keyword passes simple oblique tests but drops angle syntax.

A serif line disables common ligatures through the high-level font-variant-ligatures property. Catches: Supporting only low-level font-feature-settings passes a liga-off fixture but ignores the high-level variant property.

reference.note: The high-level property is implemented: Ironpress and WeasyPrint have matching ligature-on/off advances, while Chrome differs only in baseline placement (Chrome 10.510986pt; WeasyPrint 10.923029pt; Ironpress 11.268000pt). CSS Fonts defines the OpenType feature selection, not cross-engine baseline quantization. Raw shared-pdftoppm evidence remains reported.

description: The AVAV pair is rendered with and without kerning so the no-kerning row is visibly wider/looser. Catches: Always using the shaper defaults passes normal text tests but cannot disable kern feature application.

Two same-size lines compare default font sizing with font-size-adjust:0.8, which changes used font size to match the requested aspect value. Catches: A font-size-only implementation passes px/em/rem fixtures but ignores x-height adjustment.

reference.note: CSS Fonts defines font-size-adjust as a per-face used font-size adjustment while numeric line-height remains based on the computed size. Ironpress applies that rule: its normal-row word bounds agree with Chrome within 0.011pt horizontally and its adjusted-row bounds within 0.016pt, with the same enlarged red ParitySerif row and unchanged 48px line interval. WeasyPrint 69 reports this property unsupported, so it is not a semantic counter-oracle. Both Ironpress and Chrome PDFs are rasterized through the same pinned pdftoppm; the remaining raw contour residue comes from Ironpress CID TrueType versus Chrome Type 3 font programs, not a missing font-size-adjust operation. Raw evidence remains reported.

description: A local @font-face exposes only a regular face; font-weight:bold with font-synthesis:none must remain regular instead of fake-bolding. Catches: A renderer that always synthesizes missing bold/italic passes bold fallback tests but violates explicit synthesis suppression.

A single font shorthand declaration sets italic bold 28px/36px ParitySerif in one declaration. Catches: Parsing only longhands passes separate font-size/weight/style/family tests but drops the shorthand entirely.

An @font-face alias applies size-adjust:150% to ParitySans, making it visibly larger than a normal ParitySans row at the same CSS font-size. Catches: An @font-face parser that extracts only family/src passes basic custom-source tests but ignores metric override descriptors.

reference.note: CSS Fonts defines the @font-face size-adjust descriptor as scaling the selected face's outlines and associated metrics while retaining the computed font size. Ironpress produces the same visibly enlarged black Adjusted row and normal red row as Chrome; their word bounds agree within 0.015pt horizontally on both rows. WeasyPrint 69 reports this descriptor unsupported, so it is not a semantic counter-oracle. Both PDFs are rasterized through the same pinned pdftoppm; the residual is one-device-pixel contour coverage from Ironpress CID TrueType versus Chrome Type 3 font programs, not a missing size-adjust descriptor. Raw evidence remains reported.
